title: Exploring Interpretability in Deep Learning-Based Forest Classification - Separating Similar Forest Classes using Sentinel-2 Time Series
abstract: arXiv:2610.19270v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The ecological insurance theory posits that diverse forests are more resilient and better able to adapt to changing environmental conditions. Increasing drought and heat stress in Central Europe promotes mixed forests for maintaining ecosystem services. However, a diverse species distribution complicates remote sensing-based species mapping, as distinguishing pure from mixed species compositions at the pixel level remains challenging. We evaluated the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series and investigated the spectral-temporal features underlying class discrimination, with particular emphasis on separating pure from mixed Norway spruce pixels. We compared RNN classification models with Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and used Integrated Gradients (IG) to quantify feature attributions across spectral bands and time. translated_title: 探索基于深度学习的森林分类的可解释性——利用Sentinel-2时间序列分离相似森林类别
translated_abstract: 生态保险理论认为，多样化的森林更具韧性，能够更好地适应不断变化的环境条件。中欧日益加剧的干旱和热胁迫推动了混交林的发展，以维持生态系统服务。然而，物种分布的多样性使基于遥感的物种制图变得复杂，因为在像素级别区分纯林与混交林组分仍然具有挑战性。我们评估了循环神经网络（RNN）从Sentinel-2时间序列中进行树种分类的潜力，并研究了类别判别背后的光谱-时间特征，特别着重于分离纯挪威云杉像素与混交云杉像素。我们将RNN分类模型与随机森林（RF）和极限梯度提升（XGBoost）进行了比较，并使用积分梯度（IG）来量化跨光谱波段和时间的特征归因。表现最佳的RNN实现了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究利用循环神经网络对Sentinel-2时间序列进行树种分类，并借助积分梯度可解释性方法量化光谱-时间特征贡献，从而有效区分纯林与混交林（尤其是挪威云杉）等相似森林类别。
en_tdlr: This study uses recurrent neural networks for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series and applies Integrated Gradients to quantify spectral-temporal feature attributions, enabling the separation of similar forest classes such as pure versus mixed Norway spruce pixels.
